tagline: A winding forest road connects mountain waterfalls and a reservoir overlook.
intro: The Oscar Wigington Scenic Byway winds through Sumter National Forest along the crest of the Blue Ridge Mountains. Two lanes run between forested roadsides, with mountain turnouts and wayside picnic areas. Discover South Carolina highlights its waterfall access and the Wigington Overlook, where Lake Jocassee and the Blue Ridge Mountains fill the view. The route carries a United States Forest Service Scenic Byway designation and takes its name from a tree farmer and former mayor of Salem. SC 107 itself climbs through hilly country from SC 28 to the North Carolina border.

In 2010, South Carolina created the Falling Waters Scenic Byway, incorporating parts of the earlier corridor. The law allows those sections to retain both state and Forest Service designations. The newer designation connects northern SC 107 with S-37-413 and SC 130, extending to the North Carolina state line.

Traveling south, begin with the Wigington Overlook on SC 413, which branches from SC 107 near the North Carolina line. Along SC 107, a spur road leads to the trailheads for Spoonauger and King Creek falls. Moody Spring lies on the east side of the road just north of Cherry Hill Recreation Area. Continue toward Oconee State Park, whose entrance is near the southern end of SC 107 at SC 28.

moments.title: Wigington Overlook
moments.text: Lake Jocassee, visible from the Wigington Overlook on SC 413, is a reservoir created in 1973 by the state and Duke Power. The water covers Mount Carmel Baptist Church Cemetery, which appeared in the film Deliverance before the flooding. That site now lies beneath 130 feet of water. Four Appalachian rivers supply water to the lake: the Whitewater, Thompson, Horsepasture and Toxaway. Several waterfalls also flow directly into it, including Laurel Fork Falls and Mill Creek Falls. The dam that holds the reservoir measures 385 feet high and 1,750 feet long.
moments.notice: Look across Lake Jocassee toward the Blue Ridge Mountains.

moments.title: Kings Creek Falls
moments.text: Kings Creek Falls lies off a short spur from the Foothills Trail in Sumter National Forest. The falls lie near the Georgia line and Ellicott Rock Wilderness; their creek is a tributary of the Chattooga River. A spur road from the byway reaches trailheads for this waterfall and Spoonauger Falls. Discover South Carolina describes Spoonauger as an easy 20-minute hike and the walk to King Creek, a mile away, as more strenuous.

moments.title: Oconee State Park
moments.text: Some buildings at Oconee State Park date to the Civilian Conservation Corps, which created the park in the 1930s. The work formed part of Franklin D. Roosevelt’s civilian employment projects during the Great Depression. In 2004, fifteen cabins, the superintendent’s residence and garage, shelters, the swimming lake and bath house were listed on the National Register of Historic Places. The park also marks the southern end of the Foothills Trail and the western end of the Oconee Passage of the Palmetto Trail. Fishing and boating take place on the park’s two small lakes.
